column3: Close to the Hebrew; “consider” is rendered “Gain understanding.”
Close to the Hebrew; “above him” is rendered “beside him.”
Close to the Hebrew; אֹנוֹ (“his strength / his trouble”) is rendered “His strength,” and “for his stumbling” “at his side.”
Close to the Hebrew; “parts of his skin” is rendered “patches of his skin,” and “parts” “limbs.”
Close to the Hebrew; מִבְטַחוֹ (“his confidence”) is rendered “the shelter of his tent.”
The first line is difficult (“it dwells in his tent, what is not his”); NKJV renders “They dwell in his tent who are none of his,” and sulfur is “Brimstone.”
Close to the Hebrew; “on the face of the street” is rendered “among the renowned.”
Close to the Hebrew; אַחֲרֹנִים (“those after”) and “those before” are rendered “Those in the west” and “those in the east.”
